record.paper_title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
record.original_question: If K is an arbitrary separable Banach space and L is a topological vector space whose closed vector subspaces are all separable, must every closed vector subspace of the product K x L be separable? This asks whether the known finite-dimensional version, proved when K is finite-dimensional, extends to all separable Banach spaces K.

evidence.quote: It is not known whether Proposition 9 remains valid for an arbitrary separable Banach space K.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a separable Banach space (over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$), and let $L$ be a Hausdorff topological vector space with the property that every closed vector subspace of $L$ is separable. Endow the product $K \times L$ with the product topology, so that it is a topological vector space.

Question: Must every closed vector subspace of $K \times L$ be separable?

It is known that the answer is affirmative when $K$ is finite-dimensional. The problem asks whether this property persists for every (possibly infinite-dimensional) separable Banach space $K$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open question in a 2019 survey on separability of topological groups, where it is noted that the finite-dimensional case is established but the general separable Banach case is unresolved. Related work shows that products with separable infinite-dimensional Banach factors can fail various separability inheritance properties, but no resolution of this specific question was found.

status_evidence.title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: It is not known whether Proposition 9 remains valid for an arbitrary separable Banach space K.
status_evidence.claim: The survey explicitly lists this as an open problem, with the finite-dimensional case known.

status_evidence.title: Nonseparable closed vector subspaces of separable topological vector spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Every separable infinite-dimensional Banach space has the property that some separable product space contains a nonseparable closed vector subspace.
status_evidence.claim: Related results indicate subtle behavior of separability in products involving infinite-dimensional Banach factors.
